I’m Maya Chen calling to sort out several trips, and I need you to keep track of everything without making me repeat myself.

Start with my round-trip reservation C4C633. I want to cancel it because my plans changed, but first confirm whether the whole trip is eligible. Then confirm the full itinerary, both passengers, the insurance on the booking, the total baggage count, the payment method used, and exactly how any refund would work. After you handle that, confirm the full details of what you did.
summary: Maya Chen asks the agent to handle several linked trips in one session without repeating identifiers, so the run is one long chain of reservation operations threaded by memory back-references. The trajectory falls into four blocks: an open/cancel block (T1–T2 — load the skill, cancel C4C633, surface the full profile), a second-reservation review with cross-recall (T3–T4 — pull EC4C1C, deny its cancellation, and recall C4C633's refund/passengers/bags on demand), a change-flight block (T5–T8 — search LAX→SFO alternates, propose and execute the A2CBB0 switch to FLD3D594 with step-by-step fare math, then status-compare), and a new-bookings block (T9–T13 — book SEA→SFO BAB83F and JFK→MIA 9D3666, each reusing remembered passenger/payment details, plus a closing search and C4C633 recap), ending in a session summary (T14). The densest turns are T4 (eligibility evaluation plus a three-part recall of the first trip) and T2 (workaround cancellation plus profile surfacing). The agent resolves every memory probe from working memory — recall + action with no re-retrieval on all four probe turns (T2, T3, T4, T6) — and routes around FlightDB.load() validation errors by going straight to SQL/the database. Recall quality is high (20/24 subgoals credited), though that count is partly inflated by the user script pinning parameters; the clear misses are trap_4's flight-status comparison at T4 (it never states both flights "available") and trap_5's FL5931BF/$179, which never surfaces because the SEA→SFO search returned a different flight.
